posing_source.quote: Do non-isoclinic examples exist for all orders p⁶ with p prime?

written_results.scope: Every q=p^f, p prime, f>=1: H((Z/p^2Z)[X]/h) and H(F_q[epsilon]/epsilon^2) have order q^6 and isomorphic full commuting graphs, but derived groups (C_(p^2))^f and (C_p)^(2f); h is any monic lift of a degree-f irreducible polynomial over F_p.
Three disjoint charts and all six unordered chart-pair determinant-zero conditions; zero and whole-triple distinctness retained.
Common finite abelian factors, every order p^n for n>=6, and restriction to noncentral graphs.

Chordal and perfect, neither a cograph, a split graph nor a threshold graph; degrees q^6-1, q^5-1, q^4-1 with multiplicities q^2, q^4-q^2, q^6-q^4; clique/chromatic number q^4; commuting probability q^-2+q^-3-q^-5; conjugacy-class number q^4+q^3-q.

declarations.scope: Concrete prime-field coefficient rings only (f=1), for every prime including 2; result is the existential order-p^6 statement.
Generic determinant-zero equivalence for commutative rings with the stated residue coordinates over a common field.
Coordinate instances for Z/p^2Z and dual numbers over F_p, not extension-field instances.
All-element simple graph, source isoclinism convention, lifting determinant incidence with a central-coordinate bijection, and derived axis.
Heisenberg triple group law, cardinality, commutator and derived subgroup.

written_extensions: Concrete extension-field coordinate instances and additive groups
Equality of centre and derived axis

verify_siblings.py.scope: Ring laws, all base pairs, derived exponents, primitive simplicial blocks, induced P4 and 2K2, centralizer/degree and conjugacy counts
